claims_already_corrected_recent: AI revolutionizes / game changer for PFD application processing (06-20)
AI fisheries video / electronic-monitoring review cost-effectiveness (06-18)
North Slope gas powering data farms/crypto at 5-7 cent kWh (06-17-02)
DAF making military land available for AI data centers (06-17)
satellites don't work up here / Arctic defense sensor gap (06-15)
Alaska 30F cooler than Texas, PUE saves $150M/yr cooling (06-14)
broadband buildout = all Alaskans access high-paying tech careers (06-13)
orchestrator_note: MANY candidates this cycle orbit the data-center energy-advantage theme, which overlaps heavily with recently corrected claims (North Slope gas, cooling/PUE, broadband). Energy-abundance claims (Begich 'energy abundance', Dunleavy energy price, McCabe cooling/water) should be treated as recent-repeat-adjacent and likely fail gate point 6. The FRESHEST, most distinct angles that avoid recent repeats are: (a) Koniag/Unger $37M Army AI savings (federal contracting / ANC lane), (b) Mina rural-health RHTP 'directing us to AI' ($272M, deadline June 22 2026), (c) ADN Editorial 'no comprehensive policy' (AI governance lane), (d) CEPA Arctic-drone procurement 'fragmented, slow, risk-averse' (defense lane). The fiber-as-barrier claims (Berkowitz cul-de-sac, ACEP fiber, Dunleavy three-continents) are a distinct mechanism from the excluded gas/cooling claims and remain in play.

candidate_claims.claim_verbatim: Our AI, machine learning, and intelligent automation solutions deliver measurable impact—one current solution alone saves the Army more than $37 million annually
candidate_claims.asserter_role: Chairman and CEO, Koniag (Alaska Native Regional Corporation)
candidate_claims.claim_summary: Koniag's CEO claims the corporation's AI solutions deliver quantified federal savings at scale (>$37M/yr to the Army), positioning an Alaska Native Corporation as a credible prime AI contractor.
candidate_claims.why_load_bearing: Koniag operates under ANC 8(a) set-aside authority. The claim establishes Koniag as an AI-capable prime versus a pass-through, shaping whether DoD/federal agencies treat ANCs as genuine AI delivery partners. ANC AI sector credibility and federal AI contract flow ride on it.
candidate_claims.counter_evidence_noticed: AWS case study (https://aws.amazon.com/solutions/case-studies/us-army-koniag-gov-services/) confirms the $37M figure as 'cost avoidance' (not realized savings), via 687,000 labor hours saved annually through the DORA bot and Bedrock document generators. VP of AI Strategy Carin Chapman: 'It doesn't replace the professional. It gives them back nearly an hour each time.' Cost-avoidance vs realized-savings distinction is material to federal auditors and contracting officers.
candidate_claims.recurrence_note: Alaska Business Magazine (Dec 2025); structurally corroborated by AWS case study; Koniag subsidiary OrangeSlices AI earned a $12M DOD AI/ML contract. Not yet independently challenged in AK press.

candidate_claims.claim_verbatim: You name a program 'transformation,' but the way that the feds designed it is almost directing us to AI.
candidate_claims.asserter_role: Alaska State Representative (D-Anchorage); Rural Health Transformation Program advisory council member
candidate_claims.claim_summary: A named AK legislator on the federal rural health advisory council argues the $272M Rural Health Transformation Program's design functionally steers Alaska applicants toward AI, because funds can't be used for physical infrastructure.
candidate_claims.why_load_bearing: More than 200 Alaska entities (local govts, hospitals, tribal health orgs) are competing for $272M Year 1 (up to $1.36B over 5 yrs, second-largest state award). If the program is seen as requiring AI, it reshapes how rural health orgs and ANC health corps structure grant applications and capital plans, and pushes vendor strategy AI-first. Application deadline June 22, 2026.
candidate_claims.counter_evidence_noticed: Federal RHTP/CMS guidance does not explicitly mandate AI. Alaska DOH RHTP overview (health.alaska.gov) lists allowable uses including 'unmanned drones, remote pharmacy dispensing units, and portable diagnostic tools' — tech-forward, not AI-specific. Bipartisan Policy Center analysis: tech innovation is one of several funding pathways. Actual AK proposals include Tanana Chiefs Conference vaccine drones, wearables, VR career training. Amber Lee (Protect Our Care Alaska) argues AI 'cannot solve' underlying access/coverage gaps.
candidate_claims.recurrence_note: govtech.com (June 9, 2026) is the primary outlet; not yet widely picked up in AK press, but the underlying $272M program is live and covered by Alaska Beacon and Fierce Healthcare; deadline June 22 may drive rapid uptake. Single-source so far.

candidate_claims.claim_verbatim: Alaska has done none of that. No comprehensive policy, no clear direction
candidate_claims.asserter_role: Editorial board of Alaska's largest daily newspaper
candidate_claims.claim_summary: Alaska has taken no meaningful legislative/regulatory action on AI while 38 other states passed ~100 AI laws in 2025, leaving the state without a policy framework.
candidate_claims.why_load_bearing: Drives the argument Alaska is unprepared for AI governance, used to justify urgent legislation, a joint task force (HCR 3), and accelerated data-center policy. Capital allocators evaluating Alaska's jurisdictional/regulatory stability read the 'no policy' frame as risk.
candidate_claims.counter_evidence_noticed: 2026 session produced a deepfake/CSAM criminal bill (passed House Feb 2026, Alaska Public Media), HCR 3 establishing a Joint Legislative Task Force on AI (introduced Jan 2026, akleg.gov, text at https://www.akleg.gov/basis/Bill/Text/34?Hsid=HCR003A), and the Dept of Administration myAlaska agentic AI RFI (Dec 2025). The 'zero action' frame was partly obsolete at publication.
candidate_claims.recurrence_note: The '38 states vs Alaska' comparative framing recurs in Roger Kaye's Feb 5 and June 3, 2026 ADN pieces and Anchorage Today aggregation. ADN editorial board and Kaye are independent asserters.

candidate_claims.claim_verbatim: Procurement of Arctic-capable drones across NATO remains fragmented, slow, and risk-averse.
candidate_claims.asserter_name: Federico Borsari and Gordon B. "Skip" Davis Jr.
candidate_claims.asserter_role: Senior Fellows, Center for European Policy Analysis (CEPA); Davis is a retired U.S. Army Major General and former NATO Deputy Assistant Secretary General for Defense Investment
candidate_claims.outlet: CEPA — amplified by Defense News and DefenseScoop
candidate_claims.claim_summary: Two senior CEPA analysts assert NATO's acquisition of Arctic-capable drones is fragmented, too slow, and overly risk-averse — a critical High North readiness gap.
candidate_claims.why_load_bearing: Alaska hosts the 11th Airborne (Army's only Arctic division), JBER, Eielson, and is the primary U.S. Arctic warfare training ground. The 'fragmented procurement' narrative frames which platforms get funded/tested at Alaska installations and whether Alaska firms can compete for Arctic UAS contracts.
candidate_claims.counter_evidence_noticed: U.S. Army + drone makers ran a large-scale UAS/counter-UAS cold-weather experiment in Alaska Nov 2025. Breaking Defense (Feb 23, 2026): Quantum Systems' Vector AI drone achieved ~3 hours flight at -20 to -30F at JPMRC 26-02 near Fairbanks (https://breakingdefense.com/2026/02/frozen-tablets-and-downed-drones-armys-11th-airborne-learns-to-fight-in-the-arctic/). 11th Airborne's Lt. Col. Pearl Christensen confirmed active labs partnership to field Arctic-ready solutions.
candidate_claims.recurrence_note: Picked up by Defense News (Jan 26, 2026), DefenseScoop (Jan 22, 2026), Janes, The Watch — at least four outlets since Dec 2025.

candidate_claims.claim_verbatim: the state will remain an isolated cul-de-sac, unqualified to compete for hyperscale computing
candidate_claims.asserter_role: Co-founder, Far North Digital (trans-Arctic fiber); former Anchorage Mayor; former Alaska State Representative
candidate_claims.claim_summary: Berkowitz asserts that without fiber modernization Alaska cannot compete for hyperscale AI workloads — and his own trans-Arctic fiber project is the fix.
candidate_claims.why_load_bearing: Used to justify public/private investment in a specific trans-Arctic fiber project; shapes data-center siting decisions and the competitive landscape for existing AK telecom investment (GCI's Quintillion acquisition). Note potential conflict of interest: asserter benefits financially from his own fix.
candidate_claims.counter_evidence_noticed: GCI announced acquisition of Quintillion April 2026, adding 1,800+ miles of existing subsea/terrestrial Arctic fiber plus ~1,500 planned miles (https://www.prnewswire.com/news-releases/gci-to-acquire-quintillion-strengthening-alaskas-fiber-infrastructure-302750242.html). UAF ACEP (Feb 2024) framed fiber vulnerability/redundancy — not absence — as the gap. Berkowitz's own company page notes 'Significant fiber optic networks serve the North Slope from Fairbanks.'
candidate_claims.recurrence_note: Fiber-as-barrier framing appears in Berkowitz ADN op-ed (Jan 2026), UAF ACEP (Feb 2024), and underpins Dunleavy's April 2026 'robust fiber process' pitch. Circulates across exec, press, official slices.
candidate_claims.distinct_from_recent_repeats: partial - fiber mechanism distinct from excluded gas/cooling, but data-center-theme adjacent

candidate_claims.claim_verbatim: We have vast reserves of natural gas, significant untapped renewable potential and large-scale energy assets that are currently underutilized or stranded.
candidate_claims.claim_summary: Alaska's stranded gas and underutilized renewables give it a structural competitive advantage for AI data center investment.
candidate_claims.why_load_bearing: Policy foundation for Begich's DATA Act and Dunleavy's data-center recruitment; influences land leases, appropriations, incentives.
candidate_claims.counter_evidence_noticed: ADN (May 5, 2026): Chugach Electric 'We currently do not have gas to serve a large data center.' Golden Valley Electric: Cook Inlet gas fell from 30% to <1% of fuel supply. Stan Jones (ADN Apr 12) cites Wood Mackenzie LNG Phase 1 at $10-13.7/MMBtu vs current Cook Inlet ~$8.69. Stranded NS gas needs 3GW turbine buildout w/ 7-yr backlog.
candidate_claims.recurrence_note: Energy-abundance-as-AI-advantage echoed by Berkowitz, Schuerch, Stak Energy. Four+ asserters Jan-May 2026.
candidate_claims.distinct_from_recent_repeats: WEAK - overlaps already-corrected North Slope gas claim; likely fails gate point 6 as recent repeat

candidate_claims.claim_verbatim: Our power costs too much, and we don't have any to spare.
candidate_claims.asserter_role: former journalist and environmental advocate, Anchorage-based writer
candidate_claims.claim_summary: Alaska's electricity is too expensive and too scarce to be a viable home for power-hungry AI data centers.
candidate_claims.why_load_bearing: If accepted, forecloses the premise Alaska can compete for commercial AI infrastructure; shapes legislative decisions on recruiting operators and developing supply.
candidate_claims.counter_evidence_noticed: Jones cites Chugach 14-17c/kWh vs VA 8.99c, TX 6.12c, WA 6.61c. Counter: Stak Energy NS proposal and Cordova microgrid use behind-the-meter generation, avoiding Railbelt grid. UAF ACEP: Cordova hydro went 20-25% unused in 2025 at ~zero marginal cost.
candidate_claims.recurrence_note: Also in ADN May 5 (Chugach), Painter (Alaska Beacon Nov 2024), ADN editorial Apr 4. 4+ outlets Nov 2024-May 2026.
candidate_claims.distinct_from_recent_repeats: WEAK - data-center energy theme, adjacent to recently corrected energy claims

candidate_claims.claim_verbatim: The industry produces few jobs relative to the 'incredible demands' it places on the power grid
candidate_claims.asserter_role: former journalist, former Alaska legislative staffer, AK seafood industry leader
candidate_claims.outlet: Alaska Beacon (syndicated to Frontiersman, Homer News)
candidate_claims.claim_summary: AI data centers create very few permanent jobs relative to their massive energy demands, making them a poor economic diversification tool for Alaska.
candidate_claims.why_load_bearing: AK policymakers asked to offer land/energy/regulatory accommodations on a job-creation promise. 'Few jobs' undermines the economic rationale. Stak Energy NS proposal lists ~60 permanent jobs from a $500M facility.
candidate_claims.counter_evidence_noticed: Brookings 'New evidence on data center employment effects' (https://www.brookings.edu/articles/new-evidence-on-data-center-employment-effects/) finds local employment multiplier effects beyond direct headcount. Rep. McCabe op-ed (Apr 1, 2026) cites Quincy WA property-tax revenue. Accurate on direct headcount but may undercount indirect/construction/fiscal effects.
candidate_claims.recurrence_note: Recurs in Roger Kaye (ADN Jan 3, 2026), Alaska Center whitepaper (Jan 2026), ADN editorial (Apr 4). Painter (Nov 2024) and Kaye (Jan 2026) independent asserters.

candidate_claims.claim_verbatim: Artificial Intelligence has the potential to help the Department of Energy and our National Labs accomplish enormous challenges in the fields of science and technology, as well as offer capabilities to streamline permitting for large-scale energy and critical mineral projects in Alaska.
candidate_claims.outlet: U.S. Senator Lisa Murkowski official press release
candidate_claims.claim_summary: Sen. Murkowski frames AI as a solution to Alaska's slow permitting for energy and critical mineral projects.
candidate_claims.why_load_bearing: Permitting speed is the biggest constraint on AK resource development capital. AI-as-fix shapes federal contracting (DOE PermitAI), state response to AO 360, and project feasibility timelines.
candidate_claims.counter_evidence_noticed: DOE PermitAI / DOE AI Act early-stage, no AK-specific deployment data mid-2026. AO 360 has no timeline/funding/accountability. Structural permitting delay drivers (NEPA scope, federal land ownership, tribal consultation) are legal/jurisdictional, not information-processing bottlenecks AI resolves. No primary evidence of AI shortening an AK permit timeline.
candidate_claims.recurrence_note: Echoed in Dunleavy AO 360 (Aug 2025, near-identical language); FedScoop coverage; Alaska Business Magazine 2026 outlook. Standard AK energy-development talking point.
